licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets cleanly partition the data: fraudulent acts split into those targeting licensure procurement versus those occurring during practice; criminal conviction stands alone as a distinct legal event; impairment covers substance abuse and mental/physical incapacity; incompetence/negligence covers substandard skill-based practice failures; unprofessional/unethical conduct captures moral, ethical, and behavioral misconduct not otherwise categorized; regulatory violation covers failure to comply with statutes, rules, and board orders; prior disciplinary action covers out-of-jurisdiction sanctions; and scope/licensing violations covers practicing without or beyond a valid license or aiding unlicensed practice.

profession_specific.license_type_structu.rationale: The data clusters around credential type (licensed vs. certified), professional title (dietitian vs. nutritionist vs. combined), credential tier (full vs. provisional/temporary), and a small set of distinct types (dietetic technician, compact privilege, limited permit, nutrition associate) that fit in Other Credential.

profession_specific.alternative_credenti.rationale: The items cluster into five natural groups: the Certified Nutrition Specialist credential (BCNS/CBNS), the American Clinical Board of Nutrition Diplomate credential (DACBN), the American Board of Nutrition diplomate/membership, professional society memberships (AIN, ASCN), and the one academic-degree-based pathway (CA master's degree), together covering the full distribution without a large catch-all.

profession_specific.exempt_professions_l.rationale: These nine buckets cover the dominant patterns in the data: other licensed health professions exempt by scope, federal/military/VA carve-outs, broader government/public-agency employees (extension, schools, WIC), students and supervised trainees, dietetic technicians and paraprofessionals under supervision, persons giving only general (non-medical) nutrition information or coaching, food/supplement sales and marketing personnel, weight-control program operators, and a residual bucket for animal nutritionists, religious practitioners, home economists, researchers, and similar edge cases.

profession_specific.protected_titles.rationale: The titles cluster by credential modifier (licensed, registered, certified, or bare) crossed with professional noun (dietitian, nutritionist, or combined dietitian-nutritionist), with a separate bucket for the smaller nutrition-therapy/specialist/counselor group, one for standalone abbreviations (LD, RD, L.D., etc.), and one for the dietetic technician tier, together covering every item without an oversized catch-all.
